thread:
raj: Heads up — after a kernel roll on gpu-pool-usw2 we have ~3 nodes flip to NotReady then get tainted NoSchedule during drain. Device plugin is failing to handshake, kubelet marks GPUs as 0. I paused the rollout.
alex: Which nodes specifically? paste `kubectl describe node` and the device-plugin logs pls.
raj: nodes: gpu-usw2-3a-12, gpu-usw2-3a-15, gpu-usw2-3a-19. kubectl describe node gpu-usw2-3a-12 snippet:

```
Name:               gpu-usw2-3a-12
Role:               control-plane? no
Labels:             pool=gpu-pool-usw2
Annotations:        node.alpha.kubernetes.io/ttl: 0
Taints:             node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule
                    nvidia.com/gpu: NoSchedule
Conditions:
  Type             Status  Reason              Message
  ----             ------  ------              -------
  Ready            False   KubeletNotReady     kubelet stopped posting status: node status unknown
Allocatable:
  nvidia.com/gpu:  0
Events:
  Warning  NodeNotReady   kubelet: Kubelet stopped: handshake timeout with device plugin
```

raj: device-plugin logs (short):
```
I0323 10:12:03.123456 1 server.go:159] Starting device plugin runtime
E0323 10:12:05.987654 1 plugin.go:78] failed to initialize devices: handshake with kubelet timed out (t=10s)
E0323 10:12:06.000012 1 plugin.go:80] retrying init
```

megan: cluster-autoscaler is seeing those nodes as unready and isn't replacing them because they still report allocatable 0 and some pods are PDB-protected. CA events show `ScaleUpFailed` for gpu-pool-usw2: insufficient capacity or unready nodes present.
sam: Any kernel/dkms errors on the nodes? Looks like driver didn't rebuild after kernel bump.
raj: yes, `systemctl status nvidia-containerd` shows start failure; dmesg has: `nvidia: UVM module not found`, and dkms logs: `ERROR: Cannot find suitable kernel headers for kernel 6.1.0-rc` after the rolling update pulled a new kernel package that doesn't have matching headers in our image.
alex: That would explain the handshake — kernel module failed to insert so the nvidia device nodes never show up. Two paths: rollback kernel package on the affected nodes (reboot to old kernel), or rebuild drivers (install matching kernel-headers and rebuild dkms). Rebuild might be faster for a single node; rollback is safer for fleet.
megan: Immediate mitigation: cordon the remaining gpu nodes to stop further drains, create a temporary CPU fallback node pool for latency-insensitive jobs, and shift some workloads off GPUs. We also need to prevent CA from attempting scale-down of nodes mid-fix: add `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false`? hmm. Better: set CA `max-unready-percentage` lower or mark those nodes with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: true` until healthy.
raj: I'm going to try a hotfix on gpu-usw2-3a-12: apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r) && dkms autoinstall && systemctl restart nvidia-containerd; will report back. If rebuild fails, we'll roll back the kernel image via instance group snapshot.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 (link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-0423) — affected: gpu-pool-usw2, severity: high, assigned: @raj @alex
sam: Also worth noting: our rolling kernel upgrade config uses maxUnavailable=1 but probe timeouts + kubelet restart cause kube-controller to mark node unschedulable earlier than expected. We should tighten the prestop hooks and increase kubelet plugin handshake timeout where possible.
alex: After the dkms attempt, what do `lsmod | grep nvidia` and `kubectl get nodes -o wide` show? If device plugin reconnects it should log `Registering with Kubelet` then Allocatable GPUs != 0.
raj: Update: hotfix on gpu-usw2-3a-12 succeeded — dkms built, `lsmod` shows `nvidia`, device-plugin log: `Registered with Kubelet`, node moved back to Ready and taint removed. I'm running the same steps on 15 now. Planning fleet rollback for remaining nodes if any fail.
megan: Good. Next actions: 1) pause kernel roll-out for gpu-pool-usw2 2) surface an image build that includes matching headers or driver package pinned to avoid DKMS mismatch 3) postmortem + runbook for future kernel-driver rollouts 4) verify cluster-autoscaler config and add a guard so CA doesn't make the situation worse during kernel upgrades.
sam: Also check cost impact: if we create temporary CPU fallback nodes there's short-term cost but avoids throttling product traffic. Flag on the incident for finance review.
raj: I'll run a small canary image rebuild including linux-headers and push to image pipeline. Will update incident when done. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
alex: Nice triage. Please add the exact `dkms` command and the kernel package version to the incident notes so SRE can automate the fix.
raj: Will do — adding commands to INC-2026-0423 in a sec.
